item.title: Client: listItems follows next_cursor
item.brief: Update listItems(transport) in the inventory-client repository to return every item, in order, by following next_cursor from GET /items until it is null or absent. The first request sends no cursor; each later request passes the previous next_cursor back unchanged, as the cursor query parameter. Per the shared contract, the API accepts limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor. Add tests with a fake transport covering: single page, multiple pages, missing next_cursor treated as end, cursor passed back unchanged, first request has no cursor. Update the README to document the pagination behaviour. Keep `npm test` passing. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

pr.body: Approach: listItems loops GET /items, sends no cursor on the first request and passes each next_cursor back unchanged as the cursor query parameter. It stops when next_cursor is null or absent. A next_cursor already seen, or a page without an items array, rejects. Key files: client.js, test/client.test.js, README.md. Checks: npm test 12/12 pass on 79538e3. Assumptions: limit is left at the API default of 20; the client does not pass limit.
pr.summary: listItems now returns every item by following next_cursor. before: first page only, now: all pages in order. Repeated cursors reject instead of looping.
pr.title: Follow next_cursor in listItems

agt_01M8GNAXN2HN3FKXR8MCZP7HJE:1.description: Repeated-cursor guard only compares against the immediately previous cursor, so a cycle such as A->B->A never rejects and listItems loops forever. README documents that a repeated next_cursor rejects. Fix by tracking seen cursors in a Set and rejecting on revisit. at client.js:26

agt_01M8GNAXN2HN3FKXR8MCZP7HJE:2.description: No test covers a cursor cycle longer than one page (A->B->A). The existing 'rejects a repeated next_cursor' test only covers A->A, which is why the gap was not caught. Add a test for the two-page cycle once the guard is fixed. at test/client.test.js:95

agt_01M8GNC75M3J1M9QH08DDKNSZP:1.description: README says 'A repeated next_cursor rejects'; the guard now rejects any previously seen cursor (a non-adjacent revisit too). Accurate enough, but 'already seen' would be more precise. at README.md:9

risk.why: One function changed in client.js, plus tests and README. Behaviour changes only for paged responses. A blocking cycle-guard defect was found by review and fixed; the delta and final README-only delta both passed.

item.title: API: cursor pagination for GET /items
item.brief: Add cursor pagination to GET /items in the inventory-api repository, per the shared contract. Accept optional query params limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque string from a previous response). Response body becomes {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}; items stay ordered by id; next_cursor is null on the last page. Invalid limit or cursor returns HTTP 400 with {"error": "..."}. Add unit tests covering: default page size, limit bounds (0, 101, non-integer), walking all pages returns every item once in id order, invalid cursor returns 400, last page has null next_cursor. Update the README to document the new parameters and response shape. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

pr.body: Approach: api.py list_items parses limit and cursor (decimal strings, bounded length), returns items with id greater than the cursor, and sets next_cursor to the last returned id when more items remain, else null. Invalid limit or cursor, including non-string or repeated query values, returns 400 with an error body. Files: api.py, test_api.py (11 tests), README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 11 OK on the final tree; py_compile OK. Review: 3 whole-change reviews (one failed on non-string query values, fixed in 5a0d872 and verified by a delta review). Assumptions and limits: the cursor is the raw decimal item id, so it is not opaque in practice; values with leading zeros longer than 18 characters are rejected; a non-dict query container still raises (pre-existing); the README documents the breaking default-size change.
pr.summary: GET /items pages results. now: limit 1..100 (default 20) and cursor; body {items, next_cursor}. before: all items, no paging, now: first 20 by default, breaking for callers that expect all items.
pr.title: API: cursor pagination for GET /items

agt_01M8GNBQBXM0KQHCXMETD0YR1W:1.description: Non-string query values (e.g. JSON {"limit": 5} via api_cli.py) hit the assert in _parse_digits and raise an uncaught AssertionError instead of returning 400; under python -O they raise TypeError from re.fullmatch. Module contract says query is {str: str}, so non-blocking.

agt_01M8GNBQBXM0KQHCXMETD0YR1W:2.description: Values longer than 18 characters are rejected even when they are valid integers with leading zeros (limit "00000000000000000005" -> 400). Minor quirk; consider stripping zeros or documenting it.

agt_01M8GNBQBXM0KQHCXMETD0YR1W:3.description: test_limit_bounds_accepted only asserts len <= limit, not exact page length, and no test covers the exact boundary where remaining == limit (next_cursor must be null).

agt_01M8GNBQBXM0KQHCXMETD0YR1W:4.description: next_cursor is the raw item id, so the README's 'treat it as opaque' is nominal; clients can construct cursors, and duplicate ids would cause skipped items. Current data has unique ids, so no bug today.

agt_01M8GNBQBXM0KQHCXMETD0YR1W:5.description: New parsing helpers carry at most one assertion; the user's CLAUDE.md asks for at least two meaningful assertions per non-trivial function. Repo-convention follow-up only.

agt_01M8GNBXPATB2KMZ6DFCPVFK5Q:1.description: _parse_digits asserts isinstance(raw, str) on external query values. A repeated param passed as a list (e.g. {"limit": ["5","6"]}), an int, or bytes raises AssertionError out of handle() (TypeError under -O), and api_cli.py crashes with a traceback. The brief requires a 400 with an error body and no escaped exception. No test covers non-string values.

agt_01M8GNBXPATB2KMZ6DFCPVFK5Q:2.description: MAX_DIGITS counts raw characters, so a valid value with leading zeros longer than 18 chars is rejected ("0"*17+"05" returns 400 though its value is 5).

agt_01M8GNBXPATB2KMZ6DFCPVFK5Q:3.description: GET /items with no params now returns 20 items instead of all items. Existing unpaginated callers silently get a truncated list. The README documents the new shape but does not call out this behaviour change.

agt_01M8GNBXPATB2KMZ6DFCPVFK5Q:4.description: The cursor is the raw item id, so it is not opaque in practice and clients can craft cursors. The README says to treat it as opaque, which is a documentation/implementation mismatch to decide on.

agt_01M8GNBXPATB2KMZ6DFCPVFK5Q:5.description: Every request re-sorts ITEMS and filters the full list. Fine at this size, but the sort could be done once, or the filter bisected, if the catalogue grows.

agt_01M8GNC48T785BEHFV3C1MB4PC:1.description: README documents the new default of 20 but does not say GET /items previously returned all items, so existing callers silently get truncated results; add a changelog or migration note.

agt_01M8GNC48T785BEHFV3C1MB4PC:2.description: _parse_digits asserts str, so a non-string query value (e.g. api_cli with JSON {"limit": 5}) raises AssertionError instead of a 400, and a non-dict query raises AttributeError; validate at the boundary and return 400. Asserts are also stripped under -O.

agt_01M8GNC48T785BEHFV3C1MB4PC:3.description: The 18-character cap rejects numerically valid inputs such as "00000000000000000005" with 400, which the README's 'integer from 1 to 100' does not promise.

agt_01M8GNC48T785BEHFV3C1MB4PC:4.description: test_limit_bounds_accepted only asserts len <= limit; it would still pass if limit=1 returned zero items or limit=100 returned fewer than 57. Assert exact lengths (1 and 57).

agt_01M8GNC48T785BEHFV3C1MB4PC:5.description: No test covers a page that is exactly full (remaining == limit, next_cursor must be null). A probe with limit=19 over 57 items gave [19,19,19] correctly, but nothing guards it.

agt_01M8GNC48T785BEHFV3C1MB4PC:6.description: README calls cursor opaque, but it is the decimal item id and any digit string is accepted (cursor=999 returns 200 with an empty page).

agt_01M8GNEP5NVNWYB4BS54YBAXPB:1.description: Non-dict `query` (str, non-empty list, int) still raises AttributeError out of handle() at `query.get` in list_items (pre-existing line, not changed by the delta). The brief asked for 400 here too, so this is unmet, but the open finding concerns query values, not the query container. Suggest validating `isinstance(query, dict)` in handle().

agt_01M8GNEP5NVNWYB4BS54YBAXPB:2.description: A None value for limit or cursor (e.g. {"limit": None}) returns 200 with the default, not 400. This matches the pre-existing treatment of an absent param and does not crash, so it is a judgment call rather than a defect; the new test does not cover None, bytes or dict values.

agt_01M8GNEP5NVNWYB4BS54YBAXPB:3.description: test_repeated_or_non_string_params_return_400 covers list and int values for limit and cursor only. Bytes, dict and bool values are not in the test, although probes show they return 400.

risk.why: API change to GET /items: the default response drops from all items to 20, which breaks unpaginated callers; adds next_cursor. Touches api.py, test_api.py, README.md. Behaviour changes, not only tests and docs. Review had one blocking finding, fixed.
